risks: reserve_with_fallback | low | The claim about 'every BudgetError' being caught depends on the `BudgetError` hierarchy; if subclasses are not caught, the claim may be broken. | Check that `BudgetError` is the base class for all budget-related errors and that no other exceptions are raised by `reserve`.

handoff.purpose: Define `reserve_with_fallback` function that wraps `reserve` and returns either a reservation or a refusal envelope on `BudgetError`.

symbols.name: reserve_with_fallback
symbols.note: Public function that attempts to reserve a vendor call, returning a refusal envelope on BudgetError.

claims.text: ``(reservation, None)`` when the call may proceed, ``(None, envelope)`` when it may not.
claims.why: The code returns `(res, None)` on success and `(None, {...})` on BudgetError, matching the claim.

claims.text: FAIL CLOSED: every :class:`~daedalus.budget.BudgetError` -- refused ceiling, unreadable ledger, unobtainable lock, unpriceable vendor -- lands in the second branch.
claims.why: The `except BudgetError` clause catches any `BudgetError` and returns the second branch. The examples listed are not verified but are part of the class description.

claims.why: All paths either return `(res, None)` (success) or `(None, {...})` (exception), never `(None, None)`.

observations.what: The docstring claim about 'every BudgetError' assumes that all budget-related errors inherit from `BudgetError`. If any other exception is raised by `reserve`, it would propagate and break the fail-closed guarantee.
The function uses `reserve` and `budget_refusal_report` which are not defined in this chunk; their actual behavior could affect the correctness of the claims.
